text:
B: Hello! Kerry? Hi, hi!
A: Erm, hi. Yeah, hi. Can you hear me alright?
B: Perfect. I'm Marisol, from Leyton, East London. And you are in...?
A: Lowestoft. Suffolk. By the sea.
B: Ah, the sea! Matthew told me about Lowestoft, he grew up there. Very windy, he said.
A: Oh, did he? Yeah, it's always windy. I didn't know he was from there. That's funny.
B: Small world! So what do you do, Kerry?
A: Erm, I'm not working at the minute. I was in a warehouse, picking, six years, then they cut the shifts. So I'm looking. Shelf-stacking, cleaning, that sort of thing. Is that alright?
B: Of course it's alright! I manage a shop, a convenience store in Walthamstow. You know what? The best people I have, they are the ones who stack shelves and don't make a drama. That's gold for me.
A: Oh. Really?
B: Really. Quiet, reliable, turns up on time. My new lad, lovely, but late every single day. I would take you tomorrow, if you weren't so far.
A: Ha. That's nice of you. I get nervous in interviews, I sort of go blank, do you know what I mean. And then I'm thinking about it all night.
B: Everybody goes blank. When I came to London I was twenty-two, my English was terrible, I cleaned offices at night, in the City, ten at night to five in the morning. My first interview, I understood maybe half the questions. I just smiled and said yes to everything.
A: Oh my God. Did you get it?
B: I got it! Because I said yes to everything. Including Sundays. Mistake.
A: Ha. I'd probably do that too.
B: So tell them you're quick and you don't need watching. That's what managers want. Honestly, that's all I want.
A: Okay. Yeah. I am quick, my pick rate was always good. I'll say that.
B: Good! And for fun, what do you do?
A: Erm, walking. Charity shops. I used to do Zumba with my friend but she moved away, so I sort of stopped.
B: No! Zumba! I do Saturdays. And Leanne, the lady from Yorkshire, she does it too. We are a Zumba group now, you have to join.
A: Ha. I'd be at the back. I was always at the back.
B: The back is the best, you can copy everybody. You should go again. It's for the chat after, honestly.
A: Yeah. Maybe. It's the going on your own bit. Evenings are a bit, erm, long, living on my own. Especially in winter.
B: Ay, I understand. The dark at four o'clock, it's terrible. In Colombia it's the same time all year, six o'clock, dark, done. Here in December I want to cry.
A: Yeah, that's it. Four o'clock and you're just sat there.
B: So, Zumba, then you are tired and happy and you go home and sleep. That's my medicine.
A: Ha. Maybe. Sorry, what's that thing on your cooker?
B: The moka pot! For coffee. Everybody asks today. Do you drink coffee?
A: Erm, just instant really. Aldi's own. Sorry.
B: Kerry! No, no. Okay, I forgive you, but one day you must try
